If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to correct downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative (≥0.67 → ≤0.33) within 2 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to forecast at day 10–14.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below 80% of historical mean, apply a 1–2% upward adjustment for early horizon to align with sentiment momentum.
